And in 1969, the White House actually did a conference on this topic. And then we start to make progress toward any hunger. And then in the 1980s, and since then, we have started to backslide. And again, tens of millions of our fellow citizens are hungry. turn_text: That's wonderful, Jim. Tell me, you've been leading on the hunger issue for many, many years. Since I've known you, we go back. You've been in Congress since 1996. I think I go back at least that far with you. And I remember used to work for Joe Mokley. Where does this passion for solving the hunger issue come from on a personal level with you?

Well, actually, before I worked with Joe Mokley, I worked for Senator George McGovern. No relation, great last name. But I worked my way through college in his Senate office. at a paid internship. And he was the head of a select committee on nutrition and human needs. And he did hearings about food insecurity and hunger and lack of access to nutrition all around the country. And I get to sit in on a lot of those. And he worked, as you know, the government was a liberal Democrat, he worked very closely with Bob Dole, a conservative Republican. And they introduced and passed some of the most consequential anti-hunger pro-nutrition legislation ever in our history. And so I learned a lot about that from them. And then when I got elected to Congress, you know, people would come to my office who are looking for food. My sisters are school teachers in Worcester. They told me about kids coming to school hungry. And when they provided meals on Fridays, they were looking for meals to bring home for the weekend. because they didn't have any food. I've been to emergency rooms all throughout Massachusetts where you have senior citizens who are in the emergency room because they're taking their medication on an empty stomach when they're supposed to take it with a meal, but they can't afford their medication, their food, and their heat, and their rent. So, look. We are blessed with agricultural abundance. Hunger is a political condition. We have everything we need. What we have lacked is the political will. The point of this effort, this conference, is to just get that political will. Let's create this movement. Let's do something big and bold. Again, the last conference on this topic was in 1969. That was the time we still thought big. That was the year we led somebody on the moon. And all these years since, we have put this issue on the back burner. And as we speak, over 35 million of our fellow citizens don't know where the next meal is going to cover, and we need to do better.
